name: read-your-writes
body:
A subsequent query in a NEW process sees the mutation immediately. This is the guarantee for the direct path: when no session is live, no coordinator holds `db.lbug`, so a fresh `apg query` process opens it directly and reads the committed mutation — no session-end dependency, no explicit flush, and no prior coordination the caller must supply. When a session IS live, the same guarantee is delivered by read-through routing (`read-access-during-session`): the tool detects the session and forwards the read, so again the caller supplies no prior coordination and needs no shared in-memory state with the writer. Read-your-writes does not require the reader to know whether a session is live, nor to hold any session state.

The former "no shared session state" phrasing is dropped: with a live session the read does cross to the session process (routing), so the guarantee is "no state the caller must share" — read-through routing is transparent and is not prior coordination the caller supplies — not "no session involvement".

Acceptance: `apg node add … foo` returns, then a new `apg query` process resolving `foo` returns it — no re-scan, no explicit flush. With no live session the new process opens `db.lbug` directly on the direct path; with a live session it routes to the session.
